clauses.text: 126 THIRTY-SECOND REPORT U. S. CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION. In view of these facts the commission concurs with the department in recommending the transfer of Mr. Jett by executive order. May 14, 1915. Mr. Carroll W. Dunning may be reinstated in the Office of Markets and Rural Organization in the Department of Agriculture, where his services are needed to 3rate with the Forest Service in investigations in the marketing of woodlot Eicts. He served as statistician in forest products from November 1, 1911, to h 16, 1914, and the department states that he has had unusually valuable training; and experience at home and abroad. Since leaving the sendee he has been engaged in a marketing proposition, representing on the Pacific coast a number of eastern manufacturers, this employment being in line with his qualifications and experience. This order is issued upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Agriculture with the concurrence of the Civil Service Commission. May 25, 1915. The year limit upon eligibility for reinstatement is hereby waived to permit the reinstatement of Mr. Albert J. Phillips as associate chemist at $2,000 per annum in the service of the Bureau of Standards, Department of Commerce, at Pittsburgh, Pa. Mr. Phillips was in the service from August 13, 1906, to June 15, 1913, when he resigned. He is especially recommended by the Director of the Bureau of Standards on account of his satisfactory and efficient service. Difficulty has been experienced in obtainii^ a suitably quahfied person for filling the position. The Civil Service Commission concurs in recommending this Executive order because of Mr. Phillips lon^ and efficient service, the comparatively short period of his separation from the service, and the need of an employee with his training, which it has been difficult to meet through the usual procedure. May 27, 1915. Mrs. Burr J. Ramage may be appointed a clerk in the classified service of the Treasury Department without compliance with civil service rules. This order is issued on the recommendation of the Secretary of the Treasury, in view of the faithful aJid meritorious services of her deceased husband in the Government service, and also in view of the fact that Mrs. Ramage is without means of support. June 1, 1915. Mrs. F. Pierard may be appointed as seamstress or flagmaker at the navy yard, Mare Island, Cal., without reference to the civil service rules or navy yard regulations. Mrs. Pierard 's nusband was chief gunner's mate on the submarine F-4, which was lost in Honolulu Harbor, leaving her to support two smaU children and an invalid sister whose husband was lost on the F-4. This order is recommended by the Secretary of the Navy with the concmience of the Civil Service Commission. June 10, 1915. Mrs. Emma L. Guckert may be reinstated as an operative in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing, without regard to the length of time she has been separated from the service. This order is issued on the recommendation of the Secretary of the Treasury on account of Mrs. Guckert's former efficient service in the bureau, and for the further reason that her husband, who has been employed in the bureau since July, 1901, is sick and will probably never be able to resume his duties, and the burden of sup- porting a family consisting of the husband, wife, and two children has fallen on Mis. Guckert. June 15, 1915. The year limit upon eligibility is hereby waived to permit the reinstatement of Mr. William R. Houston as a clerk in the Railway Mail Service. Mr. Houston, who is a son of Gen. Sam Houston, governor of Tennessee, commander in chief of the Texan army of independence, president of the republic of Texas, gover- nor of the State of Texas, and United States Senator from that State, was employed in the Railway Mail Service from July 20, 1882, to May 24, 1902, when he resigned with a fair record. The Postmaster General recommends and the Civil Service Commission offers no objections to this order. Digitized by Google
